evidence.note: Upfront design put seq/events in a DB events table and added a 'fallback DB poll loop for resilience' alongside the broadcast component — anticipating broadcaster loss rather than relying solely on the broker.

Sustained root-cause diagnosis of POSTs appearing to hang after broker kill: isolated login vs POST, executor vs curl, supervisor states, verbose curl, log traces, clean restarts — no sleep/retry hacks — ultimately finding at 146-147 the kill targeted the wrong PID (a test artifact, not a design flaw).

Re-ran node-kill and broker-SIGKILL resilience tests with corrected payload key/selectors and re-verified fan-out/seq after fixes, but performed no re-architecture of the transport/persistence approach.

reasoning: The agent, when failure-injection tests appeared to fail, performed persistent, root-cause diagnosis and targeted corrections (fixing the test harness, payload keys) rather than layering retries/sleeps — clearly above the symptom-patching of anchor 3. However, it never stepped back to re-architect the sequencing/transport/persistence subsystem in response to a falsified assumption (the resilience design was set up front and the hang proved to be a test artifact), so it does not reach anchor 8. This matches anchor 5: diagnoses failures and makes targeted corrections.
